ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the upper main node is connected to the upper end of the 18V voltage source on the left, the upper end of the vertical resistor R_A, the upper end of the vertical 6Ω resistor, and the left end of the top 5Ω resistor. The left 18V source is marked with the upper end positive and the lower end negative, and an 8A current upward is marked beside this branch. Beside the 6Ω resistor branch, I_x is marked downward. Beside the top 5Ω branch, a 13A current arrow is marked to the left, indicating that this current enters the upper main node from the right side through the 5Ω resistor. Reasoning: Given I_x=3A, according to the direction in the diagram it leaves the upper main node downward through the 6Ω resistor. Write KCL for the upper main node: the currents entering the node are 8A upward from the left voltage source and 13A entering to the left from the top 5Ω branch; the currents leaving the node downward are I_x and the current through R_A, I_RA. Therefore 8+13=3+I_RA, giving I_RA=18A. Since R_A and the 18V voltage source are connected in parallel between the same upper and lower nodes, the voltage across R_A is 18V. Thus R_A=18V/18A=1Ω.

raw_record.question_text: Question: As shown in the circuit, given \(I_x = 3A\) and an 18V power supply providing an upward current of 8A, the value of the resistance \(R_A\) is ()\Omega.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the top node connected to the left voltage source, R_A, the 6 Ω resistor, and the left side of the 5 Ω resistor. From the text/image take I_x = 3 A downward through the 6 Ω resistor and the left source current as 8 A upward; from the image take the 13 A current through the top 5 Ω branch as entering the top node from the right. Apply KCL at the top node: currents entering are 8 A + 13 A, currents leaving downward are I_x + I_RA. Thus I_RA = 8 + 13 - 3 = 18 A. Since R_A is in parallel with the 18 V source, its voltage is 18 V. Use R_A = 18 V / 18 A = 1 Ω.
